pr_body:
This PR needs suggestions, especially from the Zed team. As I mentioned in a previous issue #13394 , the `vscode-json-languageserver` that Zed originally relied on has some issues with JSON schema validation on Windows, and it hasn't been updated for a long time. This PR uses the more frequently updated `vscode-langservers-extracted`, which resolves this issue.

Currently, `vscode-langservers-extracted` includes not only the JSON LSP server but also LSP servers for other languages. I think we might need a package specifically for the JSON LSP server, such as something like `vscode-json-langserver-extracted`, or we could consider using the LSP servers for other languages from this package as well. 

And, there are some issues with installing `vscode-langservers-extracted` on Windows, causing the `postinstall` script to fail. However, this does not seem to affect any functionality. Therefore, I think the best solution is for the Zed team to maintain a package like `vscode-json-langserver-extracted` or something else. This way, we can update it promptly and address the installation issues on Windows.

Any suggestions or advices are welcome.

Closes #13394

pr_comments:
For what it's worth, we already maintain our own fork of HTML language server (based on `vscode-langservers-extracted`), so I think it would make sense to maintain a fork of JSON language server as well. 
Btw. it'd be lovely if you could open an issue for this postinstall failure with HTML language server.
Thank you very much for your response. This PR is somewhat of a workaround; is it acceptable?
Yes, I think it's acceptable as is. We can look into migrating to our own fork of JSON language server eventually, but if that fixes the issue short-term, that's fine by me.
Do you want to make any other changes? This looks mergeable to me as is, so unless you want to do anything else, I'll just go ahead and merge.

This PR broke schema validation for me on macOS. Autocomplete still works, but diagnostics are missing, which is very important for our settings files.

See here: the `00000` is not highlighted as an error. The new language server here just sends `[]` back as diagnostics. If I revert this PR locally I get diagnostics back.

![screenshot-2024-07-03-09 11 58@2x](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/assets/1185253/de85799a-b243-4390-803f-9a036368cddf)


I think we should revert this for now, since Windows isn't officially supported yet and without schema validation of settings/keymaps, many users run into issues. We should also revert this in the Preview branch, since this change is already in there.
@osiewicz Thank you for diving into this issue and fix it. Sorry for introducing this bug.
No problem, that's not your fault. =)

issue_context.title: windows: The json-language-server does not support JSON schema validation
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it

Open `Zed`, open `settings.json`. On macOS, there is some kind of auto-completion supports based on json-schema. But no JSON schema validation on windows.

This is a issue of [vscode-json-languageserver](https://www.npmjs.com/package/vscode-json-languageserver) that `Zed` depends on. `vsocde-json-languageserver` relies on an older version of [vscode-json-languageservice](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-json-languageservice), which has issues with JSON schema validation on Windows. See https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/176296 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-json-languageservice/pull/177.

This issue was resolved in version `vscode-json-languageservice v5.3.2`, but since the `vscode-json-languageserver` hasn't been updated for a long time, the problem still persists.


### Environment

windows 11
